items.stem: Why must features usually be scaled before k-means?

options.text: k-means uses distances, so a large-magnitude feature would dominate
options.rationale: Correct: unscaled features distort distance-based clustering.

options.text: k-means cannot run on unscaled data
options.rationale: It runs, but gives distorted clusters.

options.text: Scaling changes the number of clusters k

options.rationale: It does not change cluster shape assumptions.

items.explanation: Correct: unscaled features distort distance-based clustering.

items.stem: Which TWO cautions apply when reading a t-SNE or UMAP 2-D plot? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Distances between far-apart clusters are not meaningful
options.rationale: Correct: these methods preserve local, not global, structure.

options.text: Cluster sizes and densities in the plot can be distorted
options.rationale: Correct: apparent size does not reflect true density.

options.text: The axes have fixed, interpretable units
options.rationale: They do not; the axes are not interpretable.

options.text: The embedding is deterministic regardless of settings
options.rationale: Results depend on parameters and initialisation.

items.explanation: Correct: these methods preserve local, not global, structure.

items.stem: A dataset has elongated, non-spherical clusters with noise. Which method fits best?

options.text: DBSCAN, which finds arbitrary-shaped dense regions and marks noise
options.rationale: Correct: density-based clustering handles shape and noise.

options.text: k-means, because it is the default

options.rationale: PCA reduces dimensions; it does not cluster.

items.explanation: Correct: density-based clustering handles shape and noise.
